set.approach: Reach the meadow camp below the Deacon, then climb to the Deacon-Matriarch col and traverse the ridgeline toward the Deacon. Drop onto snow and talus to reach the foot of the northeast face. Both lines begin beneath a big V-shaped feature at the climber's-left (east) end of the face. Sentinel Direct climbs the left fork of the V.
set.descent_text: Gain the ridge above the route and drop off it ahead of the loose, blocky towers. One rappel is followed by a traverse over looser but lower-angle, less exposed rock to the summit. Then walk the ridgeline down; cornices build over the gullies beside it, so avoid cutting across snow early in the season.

review.notes: Route page for the V start and the ridge descent; Deacon area page for the camp-to-col approach.

set.approach: Reach the East Creek basin by climbing the Bugaboo Snowpatch Col to the upper Vowell Glacier, crossing toward the Pigeon-Howser Col and descending to the East Creek Glacier. The East Creek bivy is on a rib of rock and scree, a short way below the Minaret. From camp, go directly uphill to the west face's left side. Climb the snow to the first weakness left of the major gash that splits the southwest face; depending on snow level, step across the gap to a sloping ledge to rope up on, or climb a few meters from a crack on the right.

review.notes: Route page for the camp-to-wall approach and the start; Minaret area page for the glacier approach. The route page gives no definitive descent.

set.approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Black September takes the central of three southwest-facing ribs on the central summit, between Duck a L'Orange and The Contact Zone. It starts across the gully, on the left side, from the foot of the south peak's west buttress, on polished rock with sound cracks; the first pitch is shared with Duck a L'Orange.
set.descent_text: From the west-central summit, downclimb or rappel north into the sandy col between the central and north summits. That col is the top of the third-class scrambling route: the sandy ramp angles steeply down across the north peak's west flank (gritty sand on slabs) to talus below it, and the talus leads down to the lake.

review.notes: Route page for the rib position and descent; Old Settler area page for the road and lake approach.

The start is at the southwest corner of the buttress, down and left of where Duck a L'Orange and Black September begin; there are many possible starts, all scrambly at the bottom.
set.descent_text: From the west-central summit, downclimb northward into the col shared with the north summit, then take the standard route's third-class ramps down to the talus under the west face.

review.notes: Route page for start and descent; area page for approach.

set.approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. North- and east-side routes use the Settler Creek road instead, reached from the logging camp by the Cogburn Creek forest road and a bridge; the deactivated logging road leads to a lake below the north face. The complete northwest ridge begins at a col at its toe, reached from Settler Creek or from Daiphy Lake. From Settler Creek, walk the logging road up to its switchback beneath the headwall under Settler Lake, ford the creek, bushwhack to snow and scree, and climb the big couloir to the col. From the lake, traverse meadows northwest from the outlet to the same col. Follow the crest east; the technical climbing starts at the notch below the final rise.
set.descent_text: To go down to Daiphy Lake, take the Standard Route ramp from the col between the north and central summits, or the gully on the north side of the north peak, which starts a class 4 pitch or a rappel below the summit. To go down to Settler Creek, retrace the ridge, rappelling the technical sections; the anchor above the short discontinuity is a small tree, so add a rock anchor if you can. From the col the long couloir offers a quick descent.

review.notes: Route page for the two approaches to the col and the two descents; area page for roads.

It starts across the west couloir from the West Buttress of the South Peak, in steep cracks on polished orange rock.
set.descent_text: Go down the standard scrambling ramp on the west face, starting from the col between the north and central summits.

review.notes: Route page for start and descent; area page for approach.

West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Above Daiphy Lake, climb talus to the col on the south side of the peak, then cross the broad snowfield to its southeast and contour down to the east buttress. The start is among boulders at the north side of the buttress's lower end, beneath a slabby dihedral.
set.descent_text: Downclimb the third-class ramps on the south ridge's east flank, a fourth-class chimney, and the slabs beyond it.

review.notes: Route page for approach, start and descent; area page for road and lake.

set.descent_text: Use the south peak's west-buttress descent, which goes down that peak's south ridge.

review.notes: Route page for start and the reference to the west buttress approach and descent; The south ridge descent comes from the Totally Spurious page, which defines it. Area page for road and lake.

set.descent_text: Head west along the top to the west-central summit, downclimb or rappel into the col to the north, and take the third-class ramp on the west face down to talus.

review.notes: Route page for start and descent; area page for approach.

Go by way of Daiphy Lake to the minor rib at the far right of the south peak's southwest face; higher up, the line crosses the gully leftward onto a basalt dyke and joins the crest of the West Buttress.
set.descent_text: Come down the south peak's south ridge, the way used from the West Buttress.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; area page for road and lake.

Reach the north summit's northeast ridge from Settler Creek by driving or walking the road to Settler Lake, then following the lake's north shore around and scrambling rock and heather to the ridge's lower end.
set.descent_text: To regain Settler Creek, traverse to the toe of the complete northwest ridge and descend the long couloir back to the logging road. With a car shuttle, one of the standard descents off the north summit toward Daiphy Lake is also possible.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descents; area page for roads.

set.approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Cross the talus above Daiphy Lake toward the Standard Route. This line leaves from low on that route's ramp and heads more or less straight to the north summit on the easiest ground.
set.descent_text: Return by the ramp of the Standard Route, starting at the col between the north and central summits, or by the gully down the north side of the north peak.

review.notes: Route page for approach, start and descent; area page for roads.

set.approach: Start from the Wheeler hut trailhead at Rogers Pass and take the Asulkan hut trail. Leave it at the toe of the moraine, cross the braided creek, and trend northwest over the next moraine, broken ground and slabs. Stay on top of the obvious twin moraines to reach polished slabs that lead toward the toe of the buttress. Head for the first rock step, bypassing the broken ones below it; the route begins at the top of a loose gully, where staying right avoids loose blocks.
set.descent_text: Walk out over the ridges of Mount Afton and Mount Abbott, low fifth and fourth class, down to the Abbott trail; this reverses the Asulkan traverse used on the way in. It takes heads-up downclimbing, and there is no water on the way.

review.notes: Route page and Rampart area page for the approach and start; route page for the descent.

set.approach: Reach it over the Sphinx Glacier by the Castle Towers approach, or paddle the lake to Sphinx Bay and climb from there. Then go up the glacier to the foot of the north ridge. The lower pitches are blocky scrambling, and the proper climbing begins higher up, on cracks that split the slab.

review.notes: Route page and Sphinx area page for the approach. The route page only guesses the descent, so none is written.

set.approach: Start on the lower Vowell Glacier, work up into the cirque, and bear right to the beginning of the route. The route begins on the right (east-northeast) side with easy scrambling to where the technical climbing starts, then follows the knife-edge ridge over three summits.
set.descent_text: From the third summit, rappel the ridgeline down to the glacier. Fixed rappel anchors are not to be expected, so bring slings for spikes and boulders.

review.notes: Route page only; the page notes its pitch count and grade are from memory.

set.approach: Come up the gully from the Gimli main trail; the West Ear is on the looker's left. Helix starts on the left side of the ear on grassy ledges.
set.descent_text: Descend the gully to the left of the route. It is also the bail-out line, reached by traversing left.

review.notes: Route page for the start and the gully; West Ear area page for the gully access.

set.approach: Come up the gully from the Gimli main trail; the West Ear is on the looker's left. The route is a harder finish to Helix: at the top of Helix's fourth pitch, instead of traversing left on the ramp, go right at the lower grade or a little left at the higher one, set a gear belay over a little roof, then take a crack system on to the summit.

review.notes: Route page and West Ear area page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Come up the gully from the Gimli main trail; the West Ear is on the looker's left. The line links broken cracks and corners in the gap between Helix and The Gift and begins a little to the right of Helix. Follow the Helix ledge beyond a single boulder and belay shortly past it, beneath a roof.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route on the bolted stations, which have been updated. It is possible to rappel from near the top of the fourth pitch.

review.notes: Route page for the start and rappel stations; West Ear area page for the gully access.
